_comment: Enriched Arabic glossary for translating English Web Novels, especially Chinese Xianxia/Xuanhuan, Wuxia and Korean LitRPG, Regression, Dungeon and Modern Fantasy novels.

translation_principles.consistency: Use the same Arabic term throughout a novel unless the context clearly requires a different meaning.
translation_principles.style: Prefer natural literary Arabic over literal machine translation.
translation_principles.chinese_novels: Preserve cultivation terminology and avoid replacing established fantasy concepts with unrelated Arabic concepts.
translation_principles.korean_novels: Prefer modern and readable Arabic for system, dungeon, hunter and regression terminology.
translation_principles.proper_nouns: Names of people, techniques, sects, locations and ranks should generally be transliterated or kept as proper names rather than translated literally.

rules.notes: Generic 'god' used as an intensifier/title (e.g. 'battle god', 'sword god'). Rendered as 'أسطوري' rather than a literal religious term, per replacement policy. Use 'كائن سامٍ' instead when the source genuinely means an actual deity character.
Describes power comparable to a god-tier being. Per replacement policy.
Hyphenated variant of 'god tier' (id 1). Per replacement policy.
Quality/rank classification meaning god-like grade. Per replacement policy.
Standalone adjective. Per replacement policy, rendered as 'سامٍ' rather than 'إلهي' to avoid literal religious connotation, except in compounds already covered by more specific rules above.
A god-like being/character. Per replacement policy, rendered as 'كائن سامٍ' rather than 'إله' to avoid a direct religious term.

replacement_policy._comment: Applied globally: wherever the source text uses 'god'/'divine'/'deity' as a fantasy power descriptor (not as a real-world religious reference), prefer these non-literal renderings over 'إله/إلهي' so the translation reads as fantasy terminology rather than religious language. This policy takes precedence over any conflicting older entry above.
